text:
A company made millions off her face, and when a historian asked it to help mark her grave, it said the woman never really existed. Her name was Nancy Green, the former slave who became the first Aunt Jemima at the 1893 World's Fair.

The brand's answer was that she and Aunt Jemima were not the same, because Aunt Jemima is a fictitious character. They built a fiction on top of a real woman, then used that fiction to argue they owed the real one nothing.

For ninety-seven years there was nothing there but grass.

A flat patch of it, in one of the oldest corners of Oak Woods Cemetery on the south side of Chicago, pressed against a red brick wall that runs along Sixty-Seventh Street.

Trains rattle by on the elevated tracks a few feet off, and the wall holds the noise in, so it was never a restful place to lie.

People crossed that grass for decades on their way to the famous graves deeper in the cemetery. Ida B. Wells rests at Oak Woods under tall stone, and so do Jesse Owens and the first Black mayor of Chicago.

None of them, while they lived, had a face more widely seen than the woman who lay under that bare grass by the wall.

Her name was Nancy Green. You have almost certainly met a version of her face in your own kitchen, printed on a box, your whole life, and never once been told it was hers.

She was born into slavery in 1834, on a farm outside Mount Sterling, in Montgomery County, Kentucky. No birth records were kept for enslaved children, so even her exact beginning is a guess.

By the end of the Civil War she had already buried her own husband and her own children. Freedom, when it finally came, came to a woman who had already lost almost everyone.

She went to work for a white family named the Walkers, cooking and keeping house, and when they moved north to Chicago she went with them.

That should have been the whole shape of her life. A formerly enslaved woman, cooking and cleaning in other people's homes in a cold and divided city.

Then, in 1890, a milling company came looking for her.

Here is the part the internet gets wrong almost every time, so it is worth saying plainly. Nancy Green did not invent Aunt Jemima, and she did not invent the pancake mix.

The name came from a minstrel song called Old Aunt Jemima, written and performed years before by a Black entertainer named Billy Kersands for white crowds. A flour man named Chris Rutt heard it, liked the sound of it, and slapped it onto a box of pancake flour he could not sell.

Rutt's company folded. The recipe and the name passed to the R. T. Davis Milling Company in Missouri, and Davis wanted the one thing Rutt never had.

A real woman to stand behind the made-up name.

On a judge's recommendation, they hired the family cook. Fifty-nine years old, a former slave, warm and easy with people, and exactly the image they were trying to sell.

In the summer of 1893, Chicago hosted the World's Columbian Exposition, and they put Nancy Green at the heart of it.

They built her a booth beside the largest flour barrel on earth, twenty-four feet tall. She wore the apron and the head scarf the company picked out for her.

She cooked pancakes by the hundred, and she sang for the crowds.

She told soft, pretty stories about the old plantation South, the kind the company wanted told, to white fairgoers who had come to hear exactly that.

Sit with what that actually was. A woman who had been owned, who had buried children born into bondage, standing in an apron at a world's fair, performing a happy version of slavery for the entertainment of strangers.

The fair handed her a medal for it. The company offered her a contract, and a brand was born on her back that afternoon.

For years afterward she traveled the country as the living Aunt Jemima. Thousands of appearances, at fairs and festivals and corner grocery stores, her arrival announced on billboards that put dialect in her mouth and read, "I's in town, honey."

Then came the quiet cruelty at the center of all this. The company kept the woman, and then it invented somebody else on top of her.

They wrote Aunt Jemima a whole life that had nothing to do with Nancy Green. A plantation, a kindly old master, a deep and loyal love for the white family she supposedly served, a made-up backstory printed and mailed across the country.

The face on the box was redrawn and softened and exaggerated until it was not her face at all. It became a costume the country could feel comfortable climbing inside.

And the real woman went home and kept working.

In 1910, a census taker came to her door. Nancy Green was seventy-six years old, and the record lists her job as housekeeper, in a private home, scrubbing for someone else.

Not spokeswoman. Not the most printed face in American advertising, which by then she was.

Almost no one knew. Outside her close friends and the people in her church pews, the neighbors who passed her on the street had no idea the woman in front of them was Aunt Jemima.

Because she did have a real life, and it had real dignity in it. She was a known face at Olivet Baptist Church, the oldest Black congregation in the city, a church that had sheltered people fleeing slavery when slave catchers still worked the streets of Chicago.

She lived her last years with a great-nephew and his wife. She put what small public standing she had toward the poor and toward equal rights, in a Chicago that gave Black people very little of either.

There is no evidence she ever saw real money from the empire built on her face. None that she shared in the fortune the pancake mix made, none that she was anything more than a hired performer paid for her hours.

The story that goes viral on Facebook every couple of years, the one that calls her a self-made millionaire, is not true. The proof is in the ground.

Millionaires are not buried in pauper's graves.

Now hold two things next to each other, because they happened in the same year, and the year is 1923.

That year, in Washington, the United States Senate passed a bill to build a monument on federal land in the capital. A monument to the faithful slave mammies of the South.

The proposed design showed a heavy-set Black woman cradling a white baby against her chest, while her own children reached up at her skirts for the attention she was giving the master's child instead.

This was happening right after Congress had refused, one more time, to pass a law against lynching. The country would not protect Black lives, but it was ready to carve a marble fantasy of the contented slave and set it down near the Lincoln Memorial.

It was stopped only because Black women refused to allow it. Mary Church Terrell and others organized, the Black press came down hard, and the bill died in the House.

So in 1923, America came within one chamber of Congress of putting the imaginary happy mammy in stone on the National Mall.

And in 1923, the most famous real face of that exact fantasy was standing on a Chicago street corner when a car, thrown by a collision with a laundry truck, jumped the curb and struck her.

Nancy Green died that day, at the age of eighty-nine.

They buried her in Section R3 of Oak Woods, by the brick wall, under the grass, with no stone and no name.

The fictional mammy nearly got a monument in the nation's capital. The real woman who gave that fantasy its first living face got nothing.

For nearly a century, that was where it ended.

Then a woman named Sherry Williams decided it would not end there.

Williams runs the Bronzeville Historical Society, and she gave fifteen years to Nancy Green. Fifteen years locating the exact grave, fighting cemetery rules, and hunting down a living descendant, because the law required a relative's signature before a stranger could place a headstone.

She found him. Marcus Hayes, a great-great-great-grandson living in Alabama, who said he was stunned to learn of it, since most Black families in this country cannot trace their line back that far at all.

Somewhere in those years, Williams asked Quaker Oats, the company that had owned the brand for decades and made millions off that face, whether it would help pay for a monument to the woman behind it.

The company's answer is the coldest sentence in this whole story.

Nancy Green and Aunt Jemima were not the same, they told her, because Aunt Jemima is a fictitious character.

Walk through what they were saying. The corporation took a real woman, built a fictional character on top of her, sold that character for over a hundred years, and then, when asked to honor the real one, pointed at its own invention and said she was the fiction, so nothing was owed.

In June of 2020, the brand was finally retired, and the next year it returned under a new name. Pearl Milling Company.

That was the name of the original white-owned mill from 1888, the one that started the whole thing. So even in letting her go, the company reached back past Nancy Green and named the pancakes after the men who had never made a single one.

But on the fifth of September, 2020, something else happened in that loud corner of Oak Woods by the wall.

They set a headstone on the grass at last. Granite, with a stack of pancakes etched into one side, and her name on it.

The face carved into the stone is not the face from the box. Williams chose a portrait of a younger Nancy Green in an African head wrap, dignified, looking straight ahead, because, as she put it, none of those old pictures had ever really been her.

Someone set a box of pancakes down beside the grave that day. Red handkerchiefs were tied around two potted plants, African drums played, and a pastor from her old church knelt on the ground at the marker.

Ninety-seven years late, her real name was finally the one written in stone.

The company still calls her fictitious. The grass disagrees, and so does the granite.

And now that you know it, you are one more person who can refuse to call a real woman a character. Nancy Green was here.

She cooked, she lost almost everyone, she was used, and she was never once thanked.

The least the rest of us can do is learn her real name and keep it out loud, in the kitchens where they hung her face for a hundred years and never told us whose it was.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter.
If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/AeER0VXKqi
Every coffee helps me keep creating.

text:
The wing position is all about versatility, which is what has made Alabama’s Amari Allen one of the top wing prospects in the 2027 NBA Draft. Allen is set to return for his sophomore season with the Crimson Tide after drawing a ton of interest during the 2026 draft cycle.

Last season, Allen averaged 11.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and 1.7 stocks (steals + blocks) per game while shooting 44.6 percent from the field. Allen plays a well-rounded, high-IQ style of play that will draw a ton of interest from NBA teams this cycle looking for win-now talent.

Offensively, he’s a low-mistake player. He doesn’t project as a primary creator or someone a coach can go to when they need something to happen off the dribble, but he’s smart and knows how to fit into the flow of an offense. Allen is always ready to make the extra pass or find the hole in the defense and attack it. He spaces the floor well and has good shooting mechanics that make him someone opposing defenses have to respect from outside. That respect is something Allen leveraged last year at Bama, using it to draw defenders out and then attack them on closeouts.

He has a solid finishing bag that is efficient. In the pros, he projects as a reliable catch-and-shoot floor spacer who can make a living off of corner threes or being behind the arc ready to go when the defense collapses. His athleticism and size limitations at 6-foot-6 make him someone who probably won’t ever be an elite scorer downhill, but more of a big-time connective piece on a winning team.

Allen has a great motor, and it showed in his rebounding numbers last season. He plays with a ton of effort and energy on both ends of the court, and it really shows up on the glass as he pairs it with strong rebounding skills that help him project as a potential Josh Hart-level rebounding wing in the pros.

Defensively, Allen has a good foundation. His motor, agility, and build help him project as someone who will be able to guard 1 through 3 comfortably in the pros and even some 4s depending on the matchup. With some added strength and improved discipline, Allen could become an elite two-way talent in the pros.

Allen is a well-rounded wing with still plenty of room to grow after an impressive freshman season. We see more and more that teams are really valuing IQ and versatility more than ever on the wing, and Allen offers exactly that, making him one of the top wings in this class.

text:
If you mean, “What if the United States told Cuba and Russia, if you can seize and hold part of Iran, you can keep it?”—that would be a fundamentally different proposition from supporting an Iranian opposition movement.

It would amount to offering foreign states a reward for conquering another state’s territory. Under the UN Charter, states are prohibited from threatening or using force against another state’s territorial integrity, and the UN specifically states that territory acquired through force cannot be legally recognized. 

There is also a strategic irony in your idea: if the United States offered Russia territory in Iran, Washington would be inviting a major U.S. geopolitical competitor to establish a permanent military and political presence on Iran’s territory. Offering the same deal to Cuba wouldn’t solve that problem; it would add another foreign power with its own interests.

So as a war-game thought experiment, it’s interesting because it asks: Could competing outside powers be given incentives to bear the cost of dismantling an adversary’s power? Historically, states have used alliances, economic concessions, and territorial settlements to create such incentives.

But the specific “take it and it’s yours” mechanism would be extraordinarily destabilizing—and legally incompatible with the basic rule against acquiring territory through force.

text:
I think you're comparing two different situations here, and it does not really hold up once you look at what I actually said. Asking someone to point to explicit text when nothing has been offered is one thing. That is not what happened here. I did not just demand a citation from Piers while offering nothing myself. I gave an actual case, Sherrill versus Knight, along with a more recent appellate ruling in the AP versus Trump case, both of which are real, named legal decisions with an actual holding behind them. That is a very different position from someone just saying prove it with no basis of their own.

In case you did not get a chance to read it, here is what I actually laid out in that link.

I said that there is a real legal difference depending on which part of the White House we are talking about, and that courts have already ruled on it. For the larger, generally open spaces, the press briefing room, the East Room, White House grounds broadly, once the government opens those spaces to press as a standard practice, courts have said it cannot then turn around and exclude specific outlets based on their viewpoint. That principle goes back to a 1977 case called Sherrill versus Knight, and it got reaffirmed last year when a federal judge, appointed by Trump himself, ruled that once the government opens its doors to some journalists, whether that is the Oval Office, the East Room, or anywhere else, it cannot slam those doors shut on others just because of their viewpoint.

But I also said that ruling did not survive appeal in full. A federal appeals court later overturned most of it, and specifically named the Oval Office, Air Force One, and Mar a Lago, his residence, as spaces that are not First Amendment public forums opened for general discussion. The court stated outright that the White House retains discretion to determine, including on the basis of viewpoint, which journalists get admitted to those specific spaces. The one thing the appeals court preserved was the East Room, since that is a space where all pre credentialed media is typically invited as standard practice, so viewpoint neutral access still applies there.

So my actual point was never that Trump is fully justified no matter what. I said it depends entirely on which space we are talking about. If this ban applies to the general press spaces, the briefing room, the East Room, broadly open events, that runs into the same legal wall the AP case already established. But if it is specifically about access to his office or his residence, courts have already said he has real discretion there, including the ability to exclude specific outlets based on viewpoint.

Comparing that to asking for the legal text on abortion does not really work, because that comparison only makes sense against someone demanding a citation while giving nothing themselves. I did the opposite. I gave the citation and laid out exactly how the courts have drawn the line. If you disagree with my read of those cases, I am genuinely open to hearing why. But this was not a gotcha question with nothing behind it. It was a sourced legal argument, and I would rather you engage with the actual cases than compare it to a completely separate legal debate that does not really apply here.

text:
Once the Roman government took over the Churches in Rome, (Peter didn’t create this and wasn’t your first Pope) it had to merge itself with pagan practices and beliefs in order to blend into Roman society without the masses rejecting it after hundreds of years of anti-Christian propaganda and the celebration of the killing of Christian’s. 

For centuries, Catholicism told the story of how it smashed paganism. The Roman Empire abandoned its idols, destroyed temples, and embraced the one true God. The truth? Catholicism  often dressed pagan gods up in new clothes, gave them Bible-friendly names, and put them back in the same spots they’d always been. In other words, it wasn’t a purge, it was a PR rebrand.

This isn’t wild conspiracy theory dude. Historians, archaeologists, and even some Catholic scholars will tell you the same thing. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. People don’t like letting go of their old gods, festivals, and sacred sites. 

The Roman pagan government knew that. So instead of saying, “Your god is fake, burn his temple,” it often said, “This temple? Oh, it’s for Saint So-and-So now. Keep the temple, it’s fine”

They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

Saint Barbara, the patron saint of miners.

Saint Hubertus, the patron saint of hunters and foresters.

Saint Leonhard, the protector of farmers and animals. 

Saint Nicholas, “venerated” as the patron saint of merchants and traders.

Brigid, the beloved Celtic goddess associated with fertility and healing, is perhaps the clearest example of the survival of an early goddess into Catholicism. Practitioners, mainly Ireland, pay tribute to Saint Brigid of Ireland who shares many of the early goddess’s attributes. Her feast day on the first of February falls around the same time as the pagan celebration of Imbolc.

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

This resulted through the centuries in Catholic saints replacing the old gods and goddesses.

It’s extremely clear to see former pagan gods and goddesses in Catholic saints and their attributes.

There are astonishing parallels between both belief systems, Roman paganism and aspects of Catholicism. 

The adoption of these pagan practices and symbols by the Catholic Church shows how the adoption of new institutions were difficult for pagan Romans and a blending of their pagan traditions was required for adoption of the masses after hundreds of years of the Roman government demonizing and slaughtering Christian’s. 

This all parallels the concept of diversity and multitude. In paganism, there were numerous gods and goddesses, each responsible for specific aspects of life or the world. In Catholicism, the “veneration” of saints offers a parallel system. Instead of many gods, there are hundreds of saints, each covering SPECIFIC attributes or domains. Similar to pagan gods, these saints can be both male and female.

—A large-scale New Mexico film industry of the kind that exists today would not persist without the tax credits. A much smaller version of local filmmaking would. https://t.co/chkNeMdi9H 

—Before the 2002–2003 incentive program, annual production spend was about $3 million and the crew base was roughly 100 people. After the credits arrived, spend peaked at $855 million in FY22 with 112 registered productions. Recent years have settled around $320–330 million and 76–81 projects as the global industry contracted. https://t.co/chkNeMdi9H 

—The New Mexico Film Office’s own commissioned surveys of producers find that 92–100% of the activity would not have occurred in the state without the credit. The median answer from companies was zero; out-of-state firms uniformly said none of their work would have come here. That matches how the business actually works: major productions shop locations primarily on rebate size, then secondarily on crew, stages, and travel time from Los Angeles. Every competing jurisdiction (Georgia, New York, California, Canada, the UK) offers similar or larger subsidies. Remove New Mexico’s 25–40% refundable credit and those projects move. https://t.co/HLI2T1NZKw 

—What would remain is closer to the pre-incentive baseline plus whatever unique locations and existing infrastructure can still attract. Local commercials, some New Mexico-based independent films, and occasional use of the desert or historic sites would continue. All you people do is lie. The case was handled by prosecutors in the Texas Attorney General’s office after a local recusal and a hung jury; Ken Paxton did not personally negotiate or approve the plea as a one-off favor. Here are the documented facts. https://t.co/0cYsdxlIHu 
Adam Dean Hoffman, a former Waco attorney, was arrested in June 2022 and charged with continuous sexual abuse of a young child, a first-degree felony carrying 25 years to life. The allegation was that he repeatedly abused his son’s friend over roughly three years (starting when the boy was about 7). The local McLennan County District Attorney, Josh Tetens, recused his office because Hoffman had consulted him about the case before Tetens was elected. The Attorney General’s office then took the case. https://t.co/mgz4NGGlDM 
The 2025 trial ended in a mistrial. The jury deadlocked 7-5 in favor of conviction. Prosecutors later said they were prepared to retry the case, but the child victim made clear he would not voluntarily testify a second time and preferred to move on rather than face the defendant again. Forcing testimony via subpoena would have been required for a felony conviction given the defendant’s right to confront the accuser. Without that testimony, prosecutors concluded they lacked a viable path to prove the original charge. https://t.co/1sfiv3SH65 
In April 2026 Hoffman pleaded guilty to two Class A misdemeanors: indecent assault and display of harmful material to a minor. The written confession admitted touching the victim’s genitals without consent for sexual gratification but did not specify the victim’s age. That wording meant the offenses did not trigger Texas sex-offender registration. The initial proposal from prosecutors was one day (time served from the original arrest). Visiting Judge Roy Sparkman rejected that, first raising it to 30 days plus a five-year surrender of Hoffman’s law license and a lifetime protective order. After public protests and the victim’s mother telling the court the sentence was “not enough,” the judge increased jail time to 60 days. Hoffman served 29 days and was released May 25, 2026 under the jail’s standard 2-for-1 good-behavior credit. He later registered as a sex offender in Nebraska after moving there. @2026 
Prosecutors Brenda Cantu and Dorian Cotlar, who handled the file, stated the plea secured an admission of guilt and some jail time when a felony conviction was not realistically available without compelling the child to testify again. They described the decision as made in the child’s interest. Hoffman’s own defense lawyer, Gerry Morris (who has publicly said he dislikes Paxton and is a Democrat), stated that Paxton “had absolutely nothing to do with the plea deal in this case.” Line prosecutors have said Paxton learned of the matter when it became a political issue and that he does not know Hoffman. @p 
The office’s involvement is real: it prosecuted after the local recusal and it offered the reduced charges. Characterizing it as Paxton personally “giving Hoffman a deal” as a special arrangement omits the hung jury, the victim’s refusal to testify again, the judge’s rejection and increase of the proposed sentence, and the statements from both the prosecutors and the defense attorney that Paxton was not involved in the charging or plea decisions. Those are the facts of the record.

The completion of the 3,800 km. Capricorn bioceanic corridor, connecting the Brazilian port of Santos with the Chilean ports of Antofagasta and Tarapaca, and traversing Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Chile, has sparked tremendous enthusiasm throughout the region. Leaders of all those nations, including some who are tethered to the Trump administration, as well as regional organizations representing businesses, provincial and local governments and financial entities, are engaged in lively conversation about the benefits of the corridor to their nations, how it will facilitate regional integration and expand national and international trade at a much lower cost—especially to China and the rest of Asia.

Formally launched in 2022, discussions about building it actually date back to 1960-70. It was completed in June of this year when the beautiful Bioceanic Bridge between Brazil and Paraguay over the Paraguay River was finished. Consisting of highways, bridges, border crossings, etc. Capricorn doesn’t represent the level of sophistication of the proposed Chinese-Brazilian high-speed rail corridor between Brazil’s port of Santos and Peru’s Chancay megaport. But there is a great sense of accomplishment and excitement that Capricorn is completed and offers new opportunities for the entire South American region.

Not excited was the U.S. Southern Command, whose Dialogo Americas publication warned in a fit of anti-China rage in its Sept. 4 edition that the corridor could “reinforce trade patterns that channel South American raw materials to China while regional demand for manufactures and technology of Chinese origin increases.” https://t.co/RABtq4GZ0r The publication also gnashed teeth over the Chancay port, in which China’s COSCO construction company was a major partner, as another example of the Chinese “threat” to the region.

Recent weeks and months have seen many bilateral meetings between participating governments as well as activities sponsored by Zicosur (Central Western South American Integration Zone) which brings together 70 subnational governments from Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay to discuss how the Capricorn corridor can advance regional integration, the Argentine [FM Alba website reported.]( https://t.co/623kT94dtN) The corridor’s existence also transcends political differences among the participating governments. Chile and Brazil are not on the same political wavelength, but have engaged in frequent bilateral dialogue. Chile’s Foreign Minister Francisco Perez MacKenna was in Brasilia in early August meeting with his counterpart Mauro Vieira to discuss an array of bilateral matters, including extended discussion on the Capricorn corridor.

[As reported by MSN]( https://t.co/YF9fPcobNm), Perez MacKenna reported that his government would soon become the Executive Secretary of the Capricorn Commission with “a profound sense of responsibility. We will work closely with Brazil and with the other participating countries to speed up its implementation and transform this project into a concrete tool for integration, competitiveness and development….Chile conceives of Brazil as a key ally.”

A month later, during a Sept. 7 celebration of Brazil’s Independence Day at the Brazilian embassy in Santiago, Perez MacKenna again referenced the importance of the Capricorn corridor pointing to Chile’s “historic ties” with Brazil as key to advancing regional integration. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who signed up for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s “Shield of the Americas” program even before he took office on March 11 of this year has been talking up the Capricorn corridor as well, both during recent visits to Uruguay and Paraguay, emphasizing Chile’s role as a “window to the Pacific.” The northwestern Argentine provincial governments of Salta and Jujuy which are anxious to export their mineral and mining products to China, are deeply involved in provincial and regional dialogues, including with multinational lenders, to ensure that the necessary infrastructure projects are built to facilitate trade to Chilean ports.

text:
OFFICIAL NAME:
Holy See

Note: The Holy See is the universal government of the Catholic Church and operates from the Vatican City State, a sovereign, independent territory of 0.44 square kilometers (0.17 square miles). The Pope is the ruler of both the Vatican City State and the Holy See. The Holy See, as the supreme body of government of the Catholic Church, is a sovereign juridical entity under international law.

Geography and People
Area: Total of 0.44 sq. km. (109 acres).
Population (July 2008 est.): 824 (citizens and non-citizens). Citizens: 546 (467 of which are resident).
Ethnic groups: Italian, Swiss, other.
Religion: Roman Catholic.
Languages: Italian, Latin, French, various others.
Literacy: 100%.
Work force: 3,000 lay workers (reside outside the Vatican).

Government
Type: Papacy; ecclesiastical, governmental, and administrative capital of the Roman Catholic Church.
Independence: Sovereign entity since medieval times (Lateran Pacts creating the Vatican City State and confirming independence and sovereignty of the Holy See signed with Italy on February 11, 1929).
Suffrage: Limited to Cardinals less than 80 years old.

Economy
Budget: Revenues (2007) $372 million; expenditures (2007) $386 million.
Industries: Worldwide banking and financial activities; printing; production of coins, medals, postage stamps, a small amount of mosaics, and staff uniforms. This unique, noncommercial economy is also supported financially by contributions (known as Peter's Pence) from Roman Catholics throughout the world, the sale of postage stamps and tourist mementos, fees from admissions to museums, and the sale of publications. The incomes and living standards of lay workers are comparable to, or somewhat better than, those of counterparts who work in the city of Rome.

PEOPLE AND HISTORY
Almost all of Vatican City's citizens live inside the Vatican's walls. The Vatican includes high-ranking dignitaries, priests, nuns, and guards as well as about 3,000 lay workers who comprise the majority of the work force.

The Holy See's diplomatic history began in the fourth century, but the boundaries of the papacy's temporal power have shifted over the centuries. From the 8th century through the middle of the 19th century, the Popes held sway over the Papal States, which included a broad band of territory across central Italy. In 1860, after prolonged civil and regional unrest, Victor Emmanuel's army seized the Papal States, leaving only Rome and surrounding coastal regions under papal control.

In 1870, Victor Emmanuel captured Rome itself and declared it the new capital of Italy, ending papal claims to temporal power. Pope Pius IX and his successors disputed the legitimacy of these acts and proclaimed themselves to be "prisoners" in the Vatican. Finally, in 1929, the Italian Government and the Holy See signed three agreements resolving the dispute:

A treaty recognizing the independence and sovereignty of the Holy See and creating the State of the Vatican City;
A concordat defining the relations between the government and the church within Italy; and
A financial convention providing the Holy See with compensation for its losses in 1870.
A revised concordat, altering the terms of church-state relations, was signed in 1984.

Principal Government Officials

Holy See:
Head of State--Pope Benedict XVI
Secretary of State (Prime Minister)--Cardinal Tarcisio Bertone
Deputy Secretary of State--Archbishop Fernando Filoni
Secretary for Relations with States (Foreign Minister)--Archbishop Dominique Mamberti
Apostolic Nuncio (equivalent to Ambassador) to the United States--Archbishop Pietro Sambi

The Holy See maintains an Apostolic Nunciature, the equivalent of an embassy, in the U.S. at 3339 Massachusetts Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20008, (202) 333-7121.

Vatican City State:
Head of State--Pope Benedict XVI
President of the Vatican City State Governorate--Cardinal Giovanni Lajolo

Papal Audiences
The North American College in Rome, owned and operated by the U.S. Catholic hierarchy for training American priests, handles requests for papal audiences. The address is Casa Santa Maria dell'Umilta, Via dell'Umilta 30, 00187, Rome, Italy (tel. 39-06-690-0189).

U.S.-HOLY SEE RELATIONS
The United States maintained consular relations with the Papal States from 1797 to 1870 and diplomatic relations with the Pope, in his capacity as head of the Papal States, from 1848 to 1868, though not at the ambassadorial level. These relations lapsed with the loss of all papal territories in 1870.

From 1870 to 1984, the United States did not have diplomatic relations with the Holy See. Several presidents, however, designated personal envoys to visit the Holy See periodically for discussions of international humanitarian and political issues. Myron C. Taylor was the first of these representatives, serving from 1939 to 1950. Presidents Nixon, Ford, Carter, and Reagan also appointed personal envoys to the Pope.

The United States and the Holy See announced the establishment of diplomatic relations on January 10, 1984. On March 7, 1984, the Senate confirmed William A. Wilson as the first U.S. ambassador to the Holy See. Ambassador Wilson had been President Reagan's personal envoy to the Pope since 1981. The Holy See named Archbishop Pio Laghi as the first Apostolic Nuncio (equivalent to ambassador) of the Holy See to the U.S.

The U.S.-Holy See relationship is best characterized as an active global partnership for human dignity. Establishment of diplomatic relations has bolstered the frequent contact and consultation between the United States and the Holy See on many important international issues of mutual interest. The commitment to human dignity at the core of both the U.S. and Holy See approach to the world gives rise to a common agenda for action to promote religious freedom, justice, religious and ethnic tolerance, liberty, respect for women and children and for the rule of law.

Holy See priorities for 2008 include freedom of religion, inter-religious dialogue (particularly with the Muslim world), ecumenism, protection for the traditional family, and peace (particularly for the Middle East). Pope Benedict XVI has also publicly expressed concern over the issue of climate change, describing the protection of the environment as a moral responsibility to safeguard God's creation.

Principal U.S. Embassy Official
Ambassador--Mary Ann Glendon

The U.S. Embassy to the Holy See is located in Rome in the Villa Domiziana, Via delle Terme Deciane 26, 00153 Rome, Italy, Tel: (396) 4674-3428.

The U.S. Constitution prevents foreign nations from controlling government officials primarily through the Foreign Emoluments Clause (Article I, Section 9, Clause 8) and the Ineligibility Clause (Article I, Section 6, Clause 2).The Foreign Emoluments Clause
The Rule: No person holding any "Office of Profit or Trust under the United States" can accept any present, emolument (payment or profit), office, or title from any king, prince, or foreign state without the consent of Congress.
The Purpose: The framers created this rule to stop foreign bribery, block outside influence, and keep U.S. officials loyal only to the American public.
Who it covers: Appointed officials in the executive and judicial branches, diplomats, and military officers. (There is ongoing legal debate over whether it strictly applies to elected federal officials like the president or members of Congress).
The Ineligibility Clause (No Competing Offices)
The Rule: Article I, Section 6, Clause 2 states that no U.S. senator or representative can be appointed to any civil office under the U.S. government that was created or had its pay increased during their term.
The Connection: It also prevents anyone holding a federal office from being a member of Congress at the same time. This structural separation prevents external or foreign-backed appointments from easily merging into the legislative branch.
Other Anti-Corruption Safeguards
The Oath of Office: Every major federal official must swear or affirm to support and defend the U.S. Constitution, creating a legal and moral barrier against foreign allegiance.
Treason Clause: Article III, Section 3 defines treason against the United States as adhering to their enemies, or giving them aid and comfort, ensuring severe penalties for officials who switch loyalties to external powers during wartime or conflict.

In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.

Full Text Of Pope Francis' Remarks To Congress
September 24, 2015 | by NCC Staff
Mr. Vice-President,

Mr. Speaker,

Honorable Members of Congress, Dear Friends,

I am most grateful for your invitation to address this Joint Session of Congress in "the land of the free and the home of the brave". I would like to think that the reason for this is that I too am a son of this great continent, from which we have all received so much and toward which we share a common responsibility.

Each son or daughter of a given country has a mission, a personal and social responsibility. Your own responsibility as members of Congress is to enable this country, by your legislative activity, to grow as a nation. You are the face of its people, their representatives. You are called to defend and preserve the dignity of your fellow citizens in the tireless and demanding pursuit of the common good, for this is the chief aim of all politics. A political society endures when it seeks, as a vocation, to satisfy common needs by stimulating the growth of all its members, especially those in situations of greater vulnerability or risk. Legislative activity is always based on care for the people. To this you have been invited, called and convened by those who elected you.

Yours is a work which makes me reflect in two ways on the figure of Moses. On the one hand, the patriarch and lawgiver of the people of Israel symbolizes the need of peoples to keep alive their sense of unity by means of just legislation. On the other, the figure of Moses leads us directly to God and thus to the transcendent dignity of the human being. Moses provides us with a good synthesis of your work: you are asked to protect, by means of the law, the image and likeness fashioned by God on every human face.

Today I would like not only to address you, but through you the entire people of the United States. Here, together with their representatives, I would like to take this opportunity to dialogue with the many thousands of men and women who strive each day to do an honest day’s work, to bring home their daily bread, to save money and –one step at a time – to build a better life for their families. These are men and women who are not concerned simply with paying their taxes, but in their own quiet way sustain the life of society. They generate solidarity by their actions, and they create organizations which offer a helping hand to those most in need.

I would also like to enter into dialogue with the many elderly persons who are a storehouse of wisdom forged by experience, and who seek in many ways, especially through volunteer work, to share their stories and their insights. I know that many of them are retired, but still active; they keep working to build up this land. I also want to dialogue with all those young people who are working to realize their great and noble aspirations, who are not led astray by facile proposals, and who face difficult situations, often as a result of immaturity on the part of many adults. I wish to dialogue with all of you, and I would like to do so through the historical memory of your people.

🔧 BAY PATH — BUILDING PATHWAYS FOR OUR COMMUNITIES 🎓
At our Lions Club meeting tonight, Lion Kevin Congdon welcomed Kyle Brenner, Superintendent-Director of Bay Path Regional Vocational Technical High School, along with Kirsten Congdon, Southbridge’s representative on the Bay Path School Committee.
Kyle shared an informative look at what’s happening at Bay Path and the important role the school plays in our region.
Bay Path offers 23 different vocational programs, including its newest program, Diesel Technology. These programs are developed not only to meet state requirements, but also with input from professionals who are working in the trades today. That helps students gain the practical skills and experience they need to move directly into careers or continue their education.
And the demand is certainly there. Kyle explained that Bay Path currently receives about three applications for every available seat. The existing facility limits how many students can be accepted, leaving many young people on a waiting list who would like the opportunity to attend.
Kyle also discussed a major change affecting vocational schools across Massachusetts: a new lottery-based admissions system mandated by the state. Because the system is so new, there is not yet enough information to know what its long-term impact will be on Bay Path and students from our local communities.
Bay Path’s impact goes beyond high school students. Adult education is returning, along with CTI training opportunities designed to help people who are unemployed or underemployed develop skills that can lead to good jobs and new careers.
Bay Path serves students from 10 communities, providing young people—and now more adults—with another pathway toward a successful future.
The Southbridge Lions have a special connection to Bay Path as well. Many of our own Lions are proud Bay Path graduates! 🦁
Thank you to Kyle and Kirsten for joining us, and a special thank-you to Lion Kevin Congdon for arranging an excellent and very timely program. @BayPathSuper

text:
Friday September 18, 2026

Blessings my friend!

I pray you and your family are well. I lift you up before the Lord every day! I have done this for certain people when asked, but wanted to take a moment of your time to give you a look at the finances of Liveprayer, and where we are at as we head into the final 3 ½ months of 2026.

I can’t believe this year is about over, but it has been a huge year for Liveprayer ministry wise. We celebrated 27 years online on 8/31, 23 years on TV this past March, and have ministered to more people during this year already than in any of the previous 26. As people are challenged in their individual lives, they come to a place where they realize life has to be bigger than themselves and are looking for true hope they can count on.

We have had numerous budgets over the last 27 years, but apx. 10 yrs ago cut everything we required to provide the daily ministry to people worldwide literally 24/7 to the bare bones. From day one Liveprayer has been a lean operation since I have always done the bulk of the ministry work along with our volunteer pastors who help respond to the incoming emails for prayer each day.

My business background during the decade I ran from the Lord was building a large marketing operation selling computers and various office machines to businesses thru a network of 23 telemarketing rooms around the country and Canada at the peak. However, in the early days of the ministry I saw that so many ministries who started with such pure motives, but as the Lord blessed their efforts they ended up creating a huge organization that required lots of money to exist and the focus soon went from ministry to how to use the ministry to raise money.

I vowed we would never have a building despite being offered several over the years for free. The problem is you still need to insure the building, maintain it, all things that require money. So we never left the backroom of the used car lot one of my board members owned. Sadly Clyde passed away a few years ago at 93 and his family sold the property, but we continue to operate administratively out of an adjoining property next door.

I also refused to have a huge staff since they need to be paid every Friday. That is another expense that can get out of control quickly. I also found out that if you aren’t buying multiple luxury homes, fancy cars, private jets, $5,000 designer suits, and living like the ruler of a small nation, you don’t require millions of dollars each month and the money you raise can actually go to the Lord’s work.

Here is the breakdown of our current monthly budget that is right at $55,000. For context, this is the budget of a local church with 1,000 members or less that has a few services each week along with a Bible study, prayer groups, and Sunday School classes.

-I haven’t taken an actual salary for over a decade. The ministry pays my basic monthly living expenses that totals apx. $4,000. I give my wife credit for being willing to sacrifice financial security in our later years to do the Lord’s work. While we don’t have any sort of retirement plan, stocks and bonds, and live in a home with a mortgage that still under water from the housing crisis in 2008, God has provided for our daily needs as He promised!

-My assistant who has been with my for 25 of our 27 years and our basic administrative costs come in each month around $8,000.

-My head tech who has also been with me for the last 25 years and his team who only work when needed is $10,000 a month. The truth is he could easily make 3-4x what he is paid doing the same job at a secular company.

-The TV program used to cost apx. $50,000 a month to buy the airtime, rent the studio, and pay a crew of 5 people. That expense is down to just $8,000 a month due to the fact in November of 2018 we cut all of our legacy TV contracts and went 100% streaming. With the latest software I no longer need any crew and do the program by myself. The $8,000 is for servers and bandwidth dedicated to the TV program alone.

-The largest expense each month is the bandwidth required for the website and our email operations. Sadly, we are a huge target  for hackers and when they hit us with a DDoS attack it can chew up thousands of dollars in bandwidth in minutes before we can shut the servers down and stop the attack. It is sad, but it is part of being online and preaching the Truth of the Word without compromise in a world that hates the Lord and the Christian faith. That monthly bill that can fluctuate is right around $25,000.

There you go. That is what the $55,000 we require each month covers. Virtually every dime we take in goes right to the work of the Lord and ministering to people. I have always contended it is a modern day fishes and loaves miracle! With those funds it allows us to send out the Daily Devotional each day to apx. 2.5m subscribers worldwide. It allows us to respond to the apx. 40,000 emails for prayer we receive daily. It allows me to broadcast the TV program “live” every Mon-Fri to an audience of between 20,000 and 30,000.

*THAT $55,000 EACH MONTH ALLOWS LIVEPRAYER TO IMPACT LIVES WORLDWIDE DAILY FOR THE LORD AND LEAD LOST SOULS TO FAITH IN JESUS!!!

After 27 years I have heard every method to raise funds. I settled early on in the first days of my ministry, 34 years ago, that I would use the “Paul model.” Paul was a great fundraiser because he didn’t trust in the methods and wiles of man, but shared his needs and stood in faith trusting the Lord to provide...AND HE DID! I can tell you that I still get on my knees the first of each month and lay my hands on that months budget, simply asking the Lord to provide for that month. GOD HAS BEEN FAITHFUL THOUGH HIS TIMING ISN’T ALWAYS MINE AND EVEN AFTER 34 YEAR MY FAITH WAIVERS AT TIMES.

The reason most churches and ministries focus solely on preaching to existing Christians is because most Christians at least understand the concept of giving. Very few non-Christians do, or could be expected to. Liveprayer from day one has focused primarily on reaching the lost and hurting masses outside the 4 walls of the church, making the task of raising our monthly budget an even bigger challenge.

Less than a fraction of 1% every give a dime to Liveprayer, which is fine. We aren’t here to raise money but to minister to the needs of people and lead lost souls to faith in Jesus. Also, everything we do is free and most are happy to accept what we offer which is why we do it. The Bible tells us freely you have received, freely you give. The biggest objection by non-Believers is the church and ministries are nothing but a money hustle, and sadly they are right to much of the time. We have taken that objection away.

Liveprayer has had numerous opportunities every year to clear up all of our financial challenges by renting our email data base to marketing companies who would bombard people with emails (I wouldn’t do that to my worst enemy no matter how much money it would generate!), selling everything from the latest dog food to gold bars, to more traditional avenues like writing books, holding conventions and concerts, or hosting cruises and trips to Israel. Everyone has to pray and seek the Lord about the way they raise funds, but the fact our focus is on the lost and hurting and turning Liveprayer into just another ministry/marketing operations would destroy our ability  to reach non-Christians.

Most who have supported God’s work here over the last 27 years are Believers and those few have made all God has done in tens of millions of lives worldwide possible. Also, apx. 30% of those we minister to are outside of the United States and very few ever give, but again that is fine, we are here for the sole purpose of reaching people everywhere!

Many have suggested to ask everyone to give $1. It sounds logical but anyone who has been on a church finance board or raised funds for a non-profit understands that it would be wonderful if that approach worked, but it simply doesn’t. The reality in most every church, ministry, or general non-profit is that 60%-70% of the funds come from a handful of people, the rest from others faithfully giving as they are able like the Bible teaches.

By God’s grace, over the years I have usually had anywhere from 3-10 dear friends who the Lord gave a real burden for His work here at Liveprayer and were richly blessed financially to step up at a time of need and send $5,000, $10,000, $50,000 if they were able at the moment. This has enabled me to not have to put out a plea to everyone when we are in a cash flow crunch. Traditionally during the summer months of June, July, and August donations slow down but of course the expenses don’t. This year has been especially difficult, but as we get past Labor Day each year things pick up thru the end of the year.

Sadly, since we have been doing this for nearly 3 decades now, and over that time many of our dear friends and loyal supporters have  gone home to be with the Lord. That affects the number of special friends that I can call on in a time of need. Again, by His grace the Lord has raised up new special friends to help out at a difficult time.

So, that gives you a very comprehensive look at Liveprayer from a financial standpoint. Let me share with you where we are at today and through the end of 2026. We are still trying to dig out of the hole we are in from the slow summer months. We are still dealing with the final $35,000 from our July operations and the full $55,000 from August. *I desperately need $10,000 of that $90,000 this MONDAY 9/21!  *I need the final $25,000 from July on this TUESDAY 9/22. *That clears up July, and as we approach the end of the month I need the $55,000 from our August operations between next Friday the 25th and Monday the 28th for a total of $90,000.

That $90,000 clears up the balance of our July shortfall and our August operations and gets us back on firm footing financially! I am in prayer this weekend for dear friends of Liveprayer to step up and insure we can clear up that critical $90,000 on the time table I shared with you.

During the month of October we will need to cover the $55,000 for this month, September’s operations.  During November cover  the $55,000 we require for our October ministry operations. Finally, in December with many friends making special year-end gifts, $110,000 to clear up the November operations and December’s to end 2026 with all of our operations current heading into the new year of 2027.  OUR GOD IS ABLE!!!

That is a total of $310,000 between now and the end of the year. Please stand in agreement with me that God will meet this need. I am not asking for one dime more, just the $310,000 re require between now and the end of the year. I realize that $310,000 is lots of money, but when you factor in the numbers of people worldwide Liveprayer is able to reach each day, impacting lives for Christ and leading lost souls to everlasting life through faith in Jesus, our annual budget just under $700,000 is a drop of water when you consider the overall economy of this world!

I NEED  YOU TO PRAY ABOUT HELPING ME WITH THIS IMMEDIATE NEED, AND BE PRAYING ABOUT WHAT YOU CAN  DO TO HELP ME BETWEEN NOW AND THE END OF THE YEAR!!! EVERY PERSON IS AT A DIFFERENT PLACE FINANCIALLY, GOD NEVER EXPECTS YU TO GIVE WHAT YOU CAN’T, ONLY WHAT YOU CAN!  AMEN!!!

It is sickening to watch the BILLIONS city, state, and the Federal government throw away each year. People come to this country and rip off tens, hundreds of millions of dollars in various schemes to defraud government agencies. The minions of satan raise virtually unlimited amounts of money for operations that destroy lives and lead souls to hell for eternity. God has been faithful over the last 27 years to make sure Liveprayer had the funds needed to do His work, and He won’t stop today!

The Lord has used special friends who sacrifice $10, $50, $100, $1,000, $10,000, several times over $100,000 giving as the act  of worship our giving is. All I can ask is that you keep me and Liveprayer in your prayers and stand in agreement with me for this immediate $90,000 we require over the final days of September, and the final $220,000 to end 2026 current with all of our financial obligations current.

I love you and care about you so much. Know I pray for you and your family each day. Thank you for your love, your prayers, and your faithful support of God’s work here at Liveprayer. Together we are impacting lives daily for the Kingdom of God and snatching souls from the grasp of satan and leading them to everlasting life through faith  in Jesus Christ!  AMEN!!!

*To give a gift to Liveprayer you can use your major credit card at: https://t.co/oZB3WUOGi4  or you can mail your gift to: Liveprayer, 6662 46th Ave. North, St. Petersburg, FL 33709. All gifts to Liveprayer are 100% tax deductible!

*Stocks! A great way to help Liveprayer is by donating stock. The transfer can be made in a way you get the full credit for your donation without having to pay any of the taxes you normally would on gains your stocks may have enjoyed. Contact me for information about this incredible way to help God's work here at Liveprayer: bkeller@liveprayer.com

*By the way I have been seeking the Lord since the start of this year for God to lead someone He has blessed richly to make a legacy gift of $15,000,000 to Liveprayer. That would insure that when God decides to call me home Liveprayer will continue to impact lives and lead lost souls to faith in Jesus for a minimum of 20 years. Please stand in agreement with me for the Lord to raise up that person!

*Live on after you are in Heaven!!! By remembering God's work here at Liveprayer in your will/estate planning, you can still help me share His Truth with the masses, be here for people in their time of greatest need, and help lead the lost to faith in Jesus even after God has called you home!!! God has led many of our friends in the Liveprayer family to remember His work here in their will. Please pray about this opportunity to continue and partner with me in the Lord's work at Liveprayer, even after you are enjoying your rewards and the eternal peace of Heaven! If you have any questions, don't hesitate to contact me at: bkeller@liveprayer.com

In His love and service,
Your friend, brother, and co-laborer in His work,
Bill Keller

8 Things You Need to Know about Surveillance
8 important truths about surveillance
ai-in-society
Author
Rachel Thomas

Published
August 7, 2019

Over 225 police departments have partnered with Amazon to have access to Amazon’s video footage obtained as part of the “smart” doorbell product Ring, and in many cases these partnerships are heavily subsidized with taxpayer money. Police departments are allowing Amazon to stream 911 call information directly in real-time, and Amazon requires police departments to read pre-approved scripts when talking about the program. If a homeowner doesn’t want to share data from their video camera doorbell with police, an officer for the Fresno County Sheriff’s Office said they can just go directly to Amazon to obtain it. This creation of an extensive surveillance network, the murky private-public partnership surrounding it, and a lack of any sort of regulations or oversight is frightening. And this is just one of many examples related to surveillance technology that have recently come to light.

I frequently talk with people who are not that concerned about surveillance, or who feel that the positives outweigh the risks. Here, I want to share some important truths about surveillance:

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
Data often contains errors
Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
Surveillance changes our behavior
Surveillance disproportionately impacts the marginalized
Data privacy is a public good
We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
While I was writing this post, a number of investigative articles came out with disturbing new developments related to surveillance. I decided that rather than attempt to include everything in one post (which would make it too long and too dense), I would go ahead and share the above facts about surveillance, as they are just a relevant as ever.

Surveillance can facilitate human rights abuses and even genocide
There is a long history of data about sensitive attributes being misused, including the use of the 1940 USA Census to intern Japanese Americans, a system of identity cards introduced by the Belgian colonial government that were later used during the 1994 Rwandan genocide (in which nearly a million people were murdered), and the role of IBM in helping Nazi Germany use punchcard computers to identify and track the mass killing of millions of Jewish people. More recently, the mass internment of over one million people who are part of an ethnic minority in Western China was facilitated through the use of a surveillance network of cameras, biometric data (including images of people’s faces, audio of their voices, and blood samples), and phone monitoring.

Adolf Hitler meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. in 1937. Source: Computer History
Pictured above is Adolf Hitler (far left) meeting with IBM CEO Tom Watson Sr. (2nd from left), shortly before Hitler awarded Watson a special “Service to the Reich” medal in 1937 (for a timeline of the Holocaust, see here). Watson returned the medal in 1940, although IBM continued to do business with the Nazis. IBM technology helped the Nazis conduct detailed censuses in countries they occupied, to thoroughly identify anyone of Jewish descent. Nazi concentration camps used IBM’s punchcard machines to tabulate prisoners, recording whether they were Jewish, gay, or Gypsies, and whether they died of “natural causes,” execution, suicide, or via “special treatment” in gas chambers. It is not the case that IBM sold the machines and then was done with it. Rather, IBM and its subsidiaries provided regular training and maintenance on-site at the concentration camps: printing off cards, configuring machines, and repairing them as they broke frequently.

Data is often used for different purposes than why it was collected
In the above examples, the data collection began before genocide was committed. IBM began selling to Nazi Germany well before the Holocaust (although continued for far too long), including helping with Germany’s 1933 census conducted by Adolf Hitler, which was effective at identifying far more Jewish people than had previously been recognized in Germany.

It is important to recognize how data and images gathered through surveillance can be weaponized later. Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote that “One [hard truth] is that data and surveillance networks created for one purpose can and will be used for others. You must assume that any personal data that Facebook or Android keeps are data that governments around the world will try to get or that thieves will try to steal.”

Plenty of data collection is not involved with such extreme abuse as genocide; however, in a time of global resurgence of white supremacist, ethno-nationalist, and authoritarian movements, it would be deeply irresponsible to not consider how data & surveillance can and will be weaponized against already vulnerable groups.

Data often has errors (and no mechanism for correcting them)
A database of suspected gang members maintained by California law enforcement officials was found to be full of errors, including 42 babies who had been added to the database when they were less than 1 year old (28 of whom were marked as “admitting to being gang members”). Even worse, there was no process in place for correcting mistakes or removing people once they’ve been added.

An NPR reporter recounts his experience of trying to rent an apartment and discovering that TransUnion, one of the 3 major credit bureaus, incorrectly reported him as having two felony firearms convictions. TransUnion only removed the mistakes after a dozen phone calls and notification that the story would be reported on. This is not an unusual story: the FTC’s large-scale study of credit reports in 2012 found 26% of consumers had at least one mistake in their files and 5% had errors that could be devastating. An even more opaque, unregulated “4th bureau” exists: a collection of companies buying and selling personal information about people on the margins of the banking system (such as immigrants, students, and people with low incomes), with no standards on what types of data are included, no way to opt out, and no system for identifying or correcting mistakes.

Surveillance typically operates with no accountability
What makes the examples in the previous section disturbing is not just that errors occurred, but that there was no way to identify or correct them, and no accountability for those profiting off the error-laden data. Often, even the existence of the systems being used is not publicly known (much less details of how these systems work), unless discovered by journalists or revealed by whistleblowers. The Detroit Police Dept used facial recognition technology for nearly two years without public input and in violation of a requirement that a policy be approved by the city’s Board of Police Commissioners, until a study from Georgetown Law’s Center for Privacy & Technology drew attention to the issue. Palantir, the defense startup founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, ran a program with New Orleans Police Department for 6 years which city council members did not even know about, much less have any oversight.

After two studies found that Amazon’s facial recognition software produced inaccurate and racially biased results, Amazon countered that the researchers should have changed the default parameters. However, it turned out that Amazon was not instructing police departments that use its software to do this either. Surveillance programs are operating with few regulations, no oversight, no accountability around accuracy or mistakes, and in many cases, no public knowledge of what is going on.

Surveillance changes our behavior
Hundreds of thousands of people in Hong Kong are protesting an unpopular new bill which would allow extradition to China. Typically, Hong Kong locals use their rechargeable smart cards to ride the subway. However, during the protests, long lines of people waited to use cash to buy paper tickets (usually something that only tourists do) concerned that they would be tracked for having attended the protests. Would fewer people protest if this was not an option?

In the United States, in 2015 the Baltimore Police Department used facial recognition technology to surveil people protesting the death of Freddie Grey, a young Black man who was killed in police custody, and arrested protesters with outstanding warrants. Mass surveillance could have a chilling impact on our rights to move about freely, to express ourselves, and to protest. “We act differently when we know we are ‘on the record.’ Mass privacy is the freedom to act without being watched and thus in a sense, to be who we really are,” Columbia professor Tim Wu wrote in the New York Times.

Flyer from the company Geofeedia Source
Surveillance disproportionately impacts those who are already marginalized
Surveillance is applied unevenly, causing the greatest harm to people who are already marginalized, including immigrants, people of color, and people living in poverty. These groups are more heavily policed and surveilled. The Perpetual Line-Up from the Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology studied the unregulated use of facial recognition by police, with half of all Americans appearing in law enforcement databases, and the risks of errors, racial bias, misuses, and threats to civil liberties. The researchers pointed out that African Americans are more likely to appear in these databases (many of which are drawn from mug shots) since they are disproportionately likely to be stopped, interrogated, or arrested. For another example, consider the contrast between how easily people over 65 can apply for Medicare benefits by filling out an online form, with the invasive personal questions asked of a low-income mother on Medicaid about her lovers, hygiene, parental shortcomings, and personal habits.

In an article titled Trading privacy for survival is another tax on the poor, Ciara Byrne wrote, “Current public benefits programs ask applicants extremely detailed and personal questions and sometimes mandate home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, and collection of biometric information… Employers of low-income workers listen to phone calls, conduct drug tests, monitor closed-circuit television, and require psychometric tests as conditions of employment. Prisoners in some states have to consent to be voiceprinted in order to make phone calls.”

Data privacy is a public good, like air quality or safe drinking water
Data is more revealing in aggregate. It can be nearly impossible to know what your individual data could reveal when combined with the data of others or with data from other sources, or when machine learning inference is performed on it. For instance, as Zeynep Tufekci wrote in the New York Times, individual Strava users could not have predicted how in aggregate their data could be used to identify the locations of US military bases. “Data privacy is not like a consumer good, where you click ‘I accept’ and all is well. Data privacy is more like air quality or safe drinking water, a public good that cannot be effectively regulated by trusting in the wisdom of millions of individual choices. A more collective response is needed.”

Unfortunately, this also means that you can’t fully safeguard your privacy on your own. You may choose not to purchase Amazon’s ring doorbell, yet you can still show up in the video footage collected by others. You might strengthen your online privacy practices, yet conclusions will still be inferred about you based on the behavior of others. As Professor Tufekci wrote, we need a collective response.

We don’t have to accept invasive surveillance
Many people are uncomfortable with surveillance, but feel like they have no say in the matter. While the threats surveillance poses are large, it is not too late to act. We are seeing success: in response to community organizing and an audit, Los Angeles Police Department scrapped a controversial program to predict who is most likely to commit violent crimes. Citizens, researchers, and activists in Detroit have been effective at drawing attention to the Detroit Police Department’s unregulated use of facial recognition and a bill calling for a 5-year moratorium has been introduced to the state legislature. Local governments in San Francisco, Oakland, and Somerville have banned the use of facial recognition by police.

For further resources, please check out: - Georgetown Law Center on Privacy and Technology - Digital Defense Playbook

To state the conclusion upfront: the core facts mentioned in the post—BAE Systems making secret payments to Pinochet; Thatcher publicly thanking him for his assistance during the Falklands War and crediting him with "bringing democracy"; and Thatcher, George H.W. Bush, and the Dalai Lama calling for Pinochet's release in April 1999—are all well-documented. 

BAE's Secret Payments
On September 15, 2005, *The Guardian* reported that BAE Systems had made secret payments totaling approximately $2,098,841 to Pinochet between 1997 and 2004. These funds did not go directly into Pinochet's personal accounts; instead, they were routed to a bank account in Miami and to a company registered in the British Virgin Islands—an entity Chilean authorities believed was controlled by Pinochet's financial advisor.

Some of the payments were not made in BAE's name but through Red Diamond Trading, an entity registered in the British Virgin Islands in 1998. It was established by a low-profile division at BAE's Farnborough headquarters; staff frequently traveled to Switzerland, where records of nominee contracts were kept in bank vaults. Documents indicate that these secret "commissions" were transferred via Lloyds Bank.

When asked about the purpose of the payments, BAE stated: "We do not tolerate bribery or other attempts to improperly influence the decisions of customers or suppliers. We are committed to conducting business to the highest ethical standards and to complying with the laws of all countries in which we operate."

Thatcher's Public Support for Pinochet
On March 25, 1999, Margaret Thatcher visited Pinochet—who was then under house arrest—at his mansion in Virginia Water, southwest London. She told him: "I am well aware of how grateful we are for the help you gave us during the Falklands campaign—the intelligence and communications you provided, and the sanctuary you offered to any members of our armed forces who might have drifted into Chilean territory." She subsequently added: "I am also well aware that it was you who brought democracy to Chile. You drafted a constitution suitable for democracy, you put it into effect, elections were held, and then, based on the results, you stepped down."

text:
Happy Birthday Frances Farmer

Farmer, with her patrician blonde beauty, appeared in over a dozen feature films over the course of her career and might have become a major star of the 1940s. Sadly, however, she gained greater notoriety for being committed to a state-run mental institution for five years. Frances Farmer was born on September 19, 1913, in Seattle, Washington. When she was four years old, she moved with her mother to Los Angeles. In 1935, Paramount offered her a contract, which Farmer signed on her 22nd birthday. However, she possessed a rebellious, volatile and depressive streak, which boded ill. She was cast in the B-movie “Too Many Parents” (1936), and in a lead role in the drama “Border Flight.” Later that year, Frances appeared in her first "A" feature, “Rhythm on the Range”, a musical Western starring her idol Bing Crosby. After its release, Paramount told her that “now that she was a rising star she'd have to start acting like one." Farmer was resistant, ignoring invitations to Hollywood parties and events. In an attempt to make her marketable, the studio then chose to brand her as "the star who would not go Hollywood," focusing on her "eccentric" fashion choices. (She preferred slacks and no makeup to ‘30s glamour). In 1936, she starred in “Come and Get It”. Howard Hawks was originally signed to direct, but was replaced by William Wyler midway through production; Farmer clashed with Wyler constantly and was quoted as saying that "acting with him is the nearest thing to slavery." Wyler later commented, "The nicest thing I can say about Frances Farmer is that she is unbearable.” In 1937, she appeared opposite Cary Grant in “The Toast of New York”. On set, she argued with director Rowland V. Lee and gave disparaging interviews about him to the press. Grant recalled: "She came to Hollywood knowing the rules but chose to flout them. She was self-destructive." In “Badlands of Dakota”, she starred as Calamity Jane opposite Robert Stack, and then appeared with Tyrone Power in “Son of Fury”(1942), portraying the scheming daughter of a British aristocrat in her best performance to date. From there on, it was downhill. In January 1943, Farmer assaulted a former co-worker, failed to pay the remainder of a police fine for drunk driving, and a warrant was issued for her arrest. By her own admission, she was in a poor state. On January 13, she collapsed in her room at the Knickerbocker Hotel and was apprehended there; Farmer declined to go quietly and had to be dragged through the hotel lobby kicking and screaming. She avoided jail time and was instead transferred to the psychiatric ward of Los Angeles General Hospital. There, she was diagnosed with "manic depressive psychosis.” Days later she was taken to the Kimball Sanitarium, a minimum-security psychiatric institute. Her mother took over formal guardianship, but after a fight, had Farmer committed to Western State Hospital at Steilacoom, Washington. She remained a high-security inmate there for the next five years. Farmer’s treatment was subject to significant public and critical discussion. The actress called the institution a “snake pit”, a “concentration camp”, and claimed she was physically abused. Her mental condition appears to have declined because, according to her sister, the doctors were preparing to give her a dangerous prefrontal lobotomy, but were thankfully prevented from doing so by the Farmer family attorney. On March 25, 1951, Frances was formally discharged from the jurisdiction of Western State. With her freedom restored to her, she took a job sorting laundry at the Olympic Hotel in Seattle, the same venue where she had been fêted in 1936 at the premiere of “Come and Get It.” Farmer never returned to films, though she often appeared on stage and television, and said she blamed no one for her fall. In 1970, Frances Farmer died of throat cancer at Indianapolis Community Hospital. She was only 56.
